title: 3rd Stopping Place 4th Truth 2 Kinds Of Provision

questions.question: What is the second kind of provision talked about here?
questions.answer: It is the extra kind people get used to wanting because of habit and waste.

questions.question: Is this second kind always promised to people?
questions.answer: No. Allah may give it, and He may not give it.

questions.question: What good things should a happy person hold on to when seeking food and needs?
questions.answer: Being careful, being content, and working in a halal way.

questions.question: How should a thankful person treat Allah’s gifts?
questions.answer: With thanks and appreciation.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to a person who is wasteful and greedy?
questions.answer: That person leaves halal effort, goes from place to place, and lives in misery.

questions.question: Besides the stomach, what other parts of a person need provision?
questions.answer: The heart, soul, mind, eye, ear, mouth, and other inner abilities.

questions.question: Who gives these inner and outer kinds of provision?
questions.answer: The Most Merciful Provider, Allah.

questions.question: Why were the eye, ear, heart, imagination, and mind made like keys?
questions.answer: So they can receive special gifts from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What is one example of the eye’s special provision?
questions.answer: It can enjoy the beauty and loveliness in the world.

questions.question: What helps all these human abilities benefit in the right way?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: Where does the second form of provision come from?
questions.answer: From getting used to things through habit, wasting, and using things the wrong way.

questions.question: Why can this second form seem necessary even when it is not truly needed?
questions.answer: Because a person becomes used to it.

questions.question: What makes a person blessed and happy in this passage?
questions.answer: Living simply, being content, and earning in a halal way.

questions.question: How is lawful effort described here?
questions.answer: Like worship and a prayer through action for provision.

questions.question: What does a happy person do with Allah’s blessings?
questions.answer: Accepts them thankfully.

questions.question: What causes sadness and loss in the unhappy person?
questions.answer: Wastefulness and greed.

questions.question: What wrong actions come from that bad attitude?
questions.answer: Leaving halal work, begging from many places, laziness, and harming others.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the human senses and inner gifts?
questions.answer: They also need their own kind of nourishment.

questions.question: Is the same kind of provision given to every ability in exactly the same way?
questions.answer: No. Each one gets what fits it.

questions.question: What do the eye, ear, heart, imagination, and mind open up like keys?
questions.answer: Treasures of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What is the main thing these abilities need in order to gain real benefit?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: Which kind of provision is being explained at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The second kind, which is not the true basic need for life.

questions.question: What are three causes named for this kind of provision?
questions.answer: Habit, wastefulness, and misuse.

questions.question: Does this second kind depend on a fixed promise, or on Allah’s generosity?
questions.answer: It depends on Allah’s generosity.

questions.question: What kind of lifestyle is praised as joyful?
questions.answer: A simple, content, thankful, halal way of living.

questions.question: How can careful spending and contentment become something like worship?
questions.answer: They show trust, thankfulness, and honest effort for rizq.

questions.question: What kind of person is called miserable?
questions.answer: A person who is greedy and wasteful.

questions.question: What does that miserable person do instead of proper effort?
questions.answer: He runs after many doors and lives lazily and badly.

questions.question: What parts of a person ask for provision besides the body?
questions.answer: The inner abilities and the senses.

questions.question: What effect does the right provision have on these abilities?
questions.answer: It makes them glad and pleased.

questions.question: Why was the eye especially mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that it receives beauty from the world as a gift.

questions.question: According to the end of the passage, what lets all these abilities truly gain benefit?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: What is not guaranteed in this passage?
questions.answer: The extra, made-up kind of provision that comes from bad habits and waste.

questions.question: What word in Islamic life fits “licit striving”?
questions.answer: Halal effort.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the life of someone who is content and careful?
questions.answer: Pleasant and happy.

questions.question: What should a believer feel when receiving Allah’s bounty?
questions.answer: Gratitude.

questions.question: What two bad traits lead a person away from good living here?
questions.answer: Greed and wastefulness.

questions.question: What can happen to a person’s daily life because of those bad traits?
questions.answer: It can become lazy, unfair, and unhappy.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the stomach and other human gifts?
questions.answer: Just as the stomach needs food, the other gifts also need their own nourishment.

questions.question: Name two inner human gifts in the passage that need provision.
questions.answer: The heart and the mind.

questions.question: Who prepares fitting provision for each human ability?
questions.answer: Allah, the Compassionate Provider.

questions.question: Why are human abilities described as keys?
questions.answer: Because they open the way to receive gifts from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What treasure does the eye help a person notice?
questions.answer: The beautiful sights in the universe.

questions.question: Is every strong desire a true need in this passage?
questions.answer: No. Some desires come from habit and wasting.

questions.question: What makes the second form of provision look like a real need?
questions.answer: Being used to it for a long time.

questions.question: What does the passage praise more: greed or contentment?
questions.answer: Contentment.

questions.question: How is simple living connected to happiness here?
questions.answer: It brings peace and joy.

questions.question: What kind of work should a person keep doing?
questions.answer: Lawful and proper work.

questions.question: What kind of person keeps “knocking at every door”?
questions.answer: A greedy and wasteful person.

questions.question: Why is that way of living bad?
questions.answer: It leads to laziness, wrongdoing, and sadness.

questions.question: What shows that humans need more than just food for the body?
questions.answer: Their senses and inner powers also ask for provision.

questions.question: What are some of those powers?
questions.answer: The spirit, mind, eye, ear, mouth, heart, and imagination.

questions.question: What does each one receive?
questions.answer: A fitting gift that pleases it.

questions.question: Give one example from the passage of a sense receiving its special gift.
questions.answer: The eye receives the joy of seeing beauty.

questions.question: What allows all these gifts to help a person in the best way?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: What is the difference between the second form of provision and true basic provision?
questions.answer: The second is extra and shaped by bad habits, not a real life need.

questions.question: What three things are said to produce this extra kind?
questions.answer: Addiction to habit, wastefulness, and misuse.

questions.question: Is this extra kind certain for everyone?
questions.answer: No. It is given only if Allah wills.

questions.question: What attitude makes a person truly fortunate in the passage?
questions.answer: Frugality, contentment, and thankful halal effort.

questions.question: What does the passage compare that good effort to?
questions.answer: Worship and an active du‘a for provision.

questions.question: What does a thankful person do with Allah’s favors during life?
questions.answer: Accepts them with thanks and lives happily.

questions.question: What wrong choice does the unhappy person make about earning?
questions.answer: He leaves lawful effort.

questions.question: What harmful results come from greed and waste here?
questions.answer: Running after many doors, laziness, oppression, and misery.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by mentioning the stomach first?
questions.answer: Just as the body needs food, the inner parts also need their own sustenance.

questions.question: Which human abilities are named as receiving special provision?
questions.answer: The heart, spirit, intelligence, eye, ear, mouth, imagination, and intellect.

questions.question: Why did Allah make these abilities like keys to mercy?
questions.answer: So they can open and receive many beautiful gifts.

questions.question: What is the eye’s example meant to teach about the other abilities too?
questions.answer: Each one has its own special gift from Allah, and all benefit through faith.
